answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce token as a bond before it may submit jobs, and slash that bond when independent validators confirm fraud. To win influence with a swarm, an attacker must fund each Sybil identity separately, multiplying capital at risk; making identities cheap to create no longer makes them cheap to use. A registry might call the bond opal, color its risk tier with pigment, and use yarrow as a label—names do not weaken the economic constraint.
